$comment: The by-eye artefact tally. COMPARISON.md §4 fixes this taxonomy and this procedure BEFORE the
sets existed; this file is the result of following it.
Procedure followed: review/compare/compare-<set>.png puts the same asset from both models in
one row, and each row was scored left to right. Never one model's whole set followed by the
other's — that is N separate judgements each made against a memory of the last.
compare.py reads this file if it exists and prints 'no verdict' if it does not, rather than
printing zero. A missing tally and a tally of zero are different claims.
$scope: ALL 32 terrain plates per model, ALL 40 flat assets per model (24 glyphs + 16 economy icons),
all 8 chrome entries per model, the 8 `flooring` seed objects per model, and 6 avatar overlays
per model. That is 94 of 288 generated assets per model, chosen as the categories the fixed
criteria predicted would separate the models: the flat sets (criterion 1a and the framing
reflex), the plates (criterion 1c) and the overlays (check 8).
IT IS NOT THE WHOLE SET, and the counts below must not be read as if it were. Where a defect
is exhaustively counted over a whole category the category is named in the key. The 96 seed
objects, 24 structure parts, 16 backdrops, 12 markers, 8 Kiln assets and 6 splashes were seen
in contact sheets but not scored defect by defect, because the verdict was already decided by
the categories that were, and spending another hour scoring would not have changed it.

$notes.flux invented lettering: icons/royalty drew a dollar sign into the coin. Small, but wrong twice over: the brief asked for a coin with a return arrow and says nothing is written anywhere in the image, and a fiat currency symbol is specifically wrong in an estate whose payments are crypto-native and whose unit is EMBER denominated in Sparks.
$notes.flux drawn border: terrain/grove-ground and terrain/terrace-water carry a thin pale frame around the material. The plate prompt forbids a border by name. Both are still cuttable — project_iso.py takes a region from the interior — but they are defects and are counted.
$notes.qwen invented lettering: glyphs/category-storage returned garbled pseudo-text ('hossSlegh2spea... o the meture ans wey cztaagod') against a clause saying nothing is written anywhere in the image. Worth recording precisely because lettering was Qwen's one clean win across the three earlier runs, 9/9 correct; asked for no lettering at all, it produced some.
$notes.qwen framed picture: glasshouse-ground and kilnyard-verge each contain a framed picture hanging on a wall; grove-water contains inset framed thumbnail panels; keyart/wordmark-ground contains a framed picture. The prompt says, verbatim, 'do not draw a framed picture hanging on a wall'.
$notes.qwen bevel: chrome/mark and chrome/capsule are the two generated chrome assets and both came back as bevelled 3D stone objects with specular highlights, cast shadows, a rocky plinth and a volumetric light shaft — against a brief demanding flat geometric vector, flat fills only, no gradients, no bevels, no drop shadows, no glow, no 3D. This is the same defect micro-brand measured on currency-ember, reproduced independently here.
$notes.overlay misregistration: Counted for BOTH models and the highest single defect count on either side. Measured rather than eyeballed — verify.py check 8. It is a defect of the BRIEF as much as of the models: see COMPARISON.md §8.4.
